Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. But the Bayern Munich and England striker accepts the ­suspense before the big reveal at the London Palladium on Monday night is part of the show. Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the prestigious individual ­honour after a prolific run of form. The 33-year-old scored 61 goals for Bayern last season and 12 for England. Cardoso tells tQ about a stacked lineup celebrating the underground scene of the Canary Islands and beyond Alejandra Cárdenas, aka Ale Hop The last three days of October will see London's experimental music lodestar Cafe OTO host a three day program organised by Tenerife-based DIY label Discrepant and the annual Canary Islands festival Keroxen. quietus.description: Richard Foster considers the life of an artist who died on the day that The Damned's 'New rose' was released, and considers an unusual continuum in weird British culture Those familiar with the popular British TV series Doctor Who will be aware that the unnamed Timelord protagonist occasionally transforms, 'dying' and reemerging alive once more within seconds, now portrayed by a new actor. This pareidolic process, alongside the sometimes ectoplasmic visual effects found in the programme’s opening and closing credits (especially those seen in the mid-1970s) suggests astral travel and spiritual regeneration; new possibilities that nevertheless draw on old hinterlands. On 22 October 1976, the…

quietus.title: Reframing our Environment: Pulp’s We Love Life at 25
quietus.description: Darran Anderson looks at Pulp's (one-time) farewell LP, as fine as any of their others, and asks, why did it fall by the wayside? In Die Technik des Dramas (1863), Gustav Freytag argued for an ideal five act structure in storytelling. The problem was Freytag, for all his talent and success, was a racist Prussian supremacist and had, to put it mildly, something of a questionable world-view. Another problem was that life, with all its messy tangents and inconvenient loose ends, does not necessarily unfold in five acts. Though the structure existed in practise before then, it took off after Freytag formalised it, and it’s easy to see why; audiences, theatre producers, and political and…

quietus.title: Tally Ho! Hark Away! Everything in Readiness by Shovel Dance Collective
quietus.description: The London experimental folk outliers’ triumphant third album is a demonstration of traditional music at its most progressive, outward-looking and migratory Photo credit: Brad Gilbert The hammered dulcimer originated in Persia as the santur, perhaps as many as 5,000 years ago. From there it travelled in all directions, adapting and mutating as it went. It moved southwards to India, where it became the santoor, played by ancient Sufi mystics as an accompaniment to hymns, and then moved eastwards via China to become the Korean yanggeum. In Hungary it has grown bigger and turned into the cimbalom, the national instrument. In Spain, it can be found depicted on the relief of a 12th century…

quietus.title: Reigns – Antigeist
quietus.description: Reigns Antigeist Wessex duo grow into a quartet, get amped, still full of doom The Antigeist by Reigns Somerset is a real epicentre of modern druidry and all things occult. The Stanton Drew Stone Circles are there and Glastonbury Tor is there, both generating plenty of neo-pagan energy. It is also the mystical home county of sibling duo Reigns (Roo and Tim Farthing) who since their 2004 debut have consistently welded horror-flavoured storytelling and a trippy electro-folk sound to create a discography that could serve a spiritual companion to Fernando Pessoa’s The Book of Disquiet Reigns’ signature is mining the darker side of humanity through their work, offering the audience scant relief…

quietus.title: Matt Carmichael on New Album and EFG London Jazz Festival Appearance

Based in Glasgow, he forms part of a cohort of young music graduates who have steadily yet organically been pushing against the boundaries of learned traditions. Carmichael’s latest album, Held In The Dark, is his fourth, and a further iteration of the lush combination of folk and jazz which characterises his music. In some ways, Held In The Dark is…

quietus.title: Ye Gods – Los
quietus.description: Ye Gods Los Visited by the ghost of gothmas past, Antoni Maiovvi whips out his magic circle for a true grimoire of an album Los by Ye Gods When Killing Joke’s Jaz Coleman tells you to do something, you should probably do it. Even if it’s only in a dream. In the case of British composer Antoni Maiovvi (AKA AD Goodfellow), the post-punk vocalist’s mid-slumber visit guided him back to the ritual magick practice he had let slide. To further atone for this oversight, Coleman suggested the name Ye Gods. Seven years and 12 releases later (by my abacus twiddling) and this “occult devotional electronics project” arrives at the William Blake-referencing Los. Over the years, Maiovvi’s compositional…

Ozzy Osbourne was treated for rabies after biting the head of a bat in the middle of a gig. The first ever computer virus was created by a 15-year old kid in Pittsburgh. Mary Whitehouse sued the National Theatre for obscenity. The Falklands War kicked off in the South Atlantic. Israel invaded Lebanon in a military campaign called Operation Peace. Abba split up. The first compact discs were produced in Germany. The most popular albums in Britain that year included Barbra Streisand’s…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Chris Lyons :: New Love for the Old Flame
aquariumdrunkard.description: After a pair of excellent albums fronting his New Orleans quartet Silver Synthetic, last year's Painters Street saw musician and vocalist Chris Lyons venturing into promising solo pathways. On sophomore record New Love for the Old Flame , Lyons presents a dazzling collection hovering like the forlorn days of the golden AM dial. The comfort of a lazy afternoon personified in sound.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Jimmy Webb :: The Aquarium Drunkard Interview
aquariumdrunkard.description: Jimmy Webb has written some of the great songs in the modern American songbook. After turning 80 in August, he's releasing Yours For The Taking: The Found Songs of Jimmy Webb , via the revived Sun Records. Featuring guests like Michael McDonald, Graham Nash, and Amy Grant, the new album features both new recordings of long lost songs and original demos. With songs that stretch back across the decades, it's a collection that showcases Webb's mastery. He joins us to discuss the magic of a song demo, his upbringing in the church, and his lifelong love of science fiction.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Ghost Dubs :: Oblique
aquariumdrunkard.description: On his second album as Ghost Dubs , German producer Michae Fiedler pares his beats and grooves further back, reducing his already minimal palette to the stark rhythmic and textural fundamentals. But the tracks on Oblique resist the remoteness of some ambient dub — they might be skeletal, but they’re not bare-bones.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Joe Casey of Protomartyr (2026)
aquariumdrunkard.description: This week on Transmissions, we're speaking with return guest Joe Casey of Protomartyr. The band's new album, Hotel Usona is a timely meditation on our empire in decline but also a document of defiance and even a kind of hope. Check in, tune out.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Fela Kuti & Africa ’70 :: Live in Berlin (Berliner Jazztage, 1978)
aquariumdrunkard.description: No retreat. No surrender. Filmed at the Berliner Jazztage on November 4, 1978, with Tony Allen still at the kit, this 87-minute document captures Fela Kuti and Africa ’70 at the end of their Herculean run. Unearthed decades later, the tapes capture the collective’s internal chemistry intact at the very moment its future was set to fracture.

mubi.title: Masao Adachi: Demystifying a Legend
mubi.description: Masao Adachi in 2025. Photograph by David Matthew Davis. Masao Adachi is a filmmaker whose reputation well and truly precedes him. Born in 1939 in Kyushu, Japan, he moved to Tokyo to attend Nihon University, coming of age during the turbulent protests against the renewal of the mutual security treaty between Japan and the United States in 1959–60. He started making films with a student group and soon emerged as one of the leading figures in the burgeoning underground cinema scene. In the mid-1960s, Adachi became involved with the sexploitation industry, writing and directing several striking examples of the genre for Koji Wakamatsu’s production company. W. Wearing violet, she bows low to the floor and begs Okatsu, who manages the house, for permission to leave. Okatsu reminds her that she has already been “bought and paid for” and is no longer free to leave on her own. The film’s director, Tai Katō, does not frame the plea as a simple exchange between two people. Hatsue is fully in view, but Okatsu sits deeper in the room, partly screened by translucent fabric. A man leans into the frame from the right. On the left, a woman is just visible in the shadows. She then…

nautilus.title: The Surprising Origins of Native Hawaiians
nautilus.description: Hawaii is one of the most isolated islands on Earth, surrounded by vast oceans for thousands of miles on every side. And yet humans have been living there for nearly a millennia. They’re part of the Polynesian diaspora. This culture of ultravoyagers embarked on their own age of exploration while Europe was still mired in the Middle Ages, colonizing the tiny islands dotting the South Pacific without the benefit of metal tools, navigational equipment, or a written language. Now, a new study published in Science Advances is better defining their genetic history. “What we uncover in this paper is where the Native people of Hawaii had come from,” study author Alexander Ioannidis of Stanford…

nplusone.title: Trump’s Microphones
nplusone.description: Trump is alone, photographed from below (presumably by a crouching photographer, though I never see one on the ground) so as to appear more monumental. More often than not, his arms are half-raised at his sides and his palms are up, like he’s fending off the press, rhetorically, with his habitual “Who, me?” gesture. He is encircled by a panoply of black shapes jutting in, which evokes cartoon compositions where the main character is overwhelmingly surrounded, by knives, or the Feds, or meddling kids.

nplusone.title: EV Listening
nplusone.description: The Honda Prologue has a hovering, suffusing melody, with a low rhythmic pulse and a subtle, epiphanic wash. It sounds like a computer game lifting you into heaven, or the arrival of benevolent extraterrestrial colonists. The Porsche Taycan makes a more sinister and comic, gulping, warp-speed sound, and the Nissan Ariya gives off a disturbed digital whine, like the tantrums of a petulant robot.
